event_summary: Nashville Noticias reporter Estefany Rodriguez Florez was detained by ICE following a traffic stop. Her lawyers challenged the detention and alleged agents did not present an arrest warrant; ICE disputed the no-warrant characterization in a court filing.
outcome: Detention interrupted reporting and led to a legal challenge.
organizational_response: Legal challenge filed; journalism and press-freedom organizations publicly raised concerns.
notes: Migration from v1 preserves factual dispute and does not infer motive or immigration status.

actor_named: law-enforcement and crowd actors as described by outlet
event_summary: Founder Maritza Félix publicly described Conecta Arizona reporters experiencing violence while covering protests, including pepper spray, as well as racialized verbal harassment from counter-protesters.
outcome: The newsroom changed safety practices in response to documented exposure.
organizational_response: Paired reporting; contingency planning; safety training for Conecta Arizona and other local reporters.
notes: Broad episode range retained because exact incident dates are not consistently specified. Harassment component may later be split into a separate informational event.

event_summary: El Tímpano publicly changed reporting practices to reduce risks to undocumented immigrant sources as immigration-enforcement concerns increased.
outcome: Reporting and source-protection practices were modified to reduce exposure.
organizational_response: Adjusted reporting and source-protection practices to reduce exposure of sensitive identifying information.
notes: Coded as anticipatory response rather than an attack on the outlet.

event_summary: Investigative reporter Lexis-Olivier Ray was reported pepper-sprayed and shoved while covering an immigration-enforcement protest and reported being struck or threatened with additional projectiles or arrest during subsequent coverage.
outcome: Physical force and threat of arrest interrupted reporting.
organizational_response: Publicly documented incident; organizational response not yet coded.
notes: External comparison case unless later crosswalk review links LA TACO to the national frame.

notes: Structural exposure only; not evidence every mapped outlet experienced the same decline.

event_summary: Press-freedom organizations documented multiple incidents involving federal agents using pepper spray, tear gas, stun grenades, and crowd-control munitions against journalists covering immigration enforcement in Minnesota. CPJ and IWMF subsequently launched a rapid-response fund with an initial Minnesota focus.
outcome: Statewide safety exposure generated emergency-support responses.
organizational_response: Emergency support infrastructure created at the sector/state level.
notes: Statewide sector exposure; do not assign to a mapped Minnesota outlet without outlet-specific evidence.

actor_named: internal organizational and employment conditions under dispute
event_summary: Mission Local reported that seven people left El Tecolote between March and early September 2026, including the editor-in-chief, with one original newsroom employee remaining from the editorial team that began the year. Former staff described stalled contracts and operational problems; Acción Latina leadership disputed attributing departures uniformly to management or workplace concerns.
outcome: Documented staff loss reduced editorial capacity and slowed publishing.
organizational_response: Founder stepped in as interim editor; freelance contributors continued publishing; organization stated it was hiring a new editor and remained committed to serving the community.
notes: Causal explanations remain disputed; coding is limited to documented staffing and publishing consequences.

outcome: The planned field assignment was cancelled to reduce legal and personal exposure.
organizational_response: Newsroom conducted a risk assessment and cancelled the field assignment.
